question: How does the FOR NO KEY UPDATE row-level lock mode differ from FOR UPDATE?
expected_answer: It is weaker: it does not block SELECT FOR KEY SHARE commands that try to lock the same rows.

spans.quote:
FOR NO KEY UPDATE
Behaves similarly to FOR UPDATE, except that the lock acquired is weaker: this lock will not block
SELECT FOR KEY SHARE commands that attempt to acquire a lock on the same rows.

question: Which DDL commands are not MVCC-safe in PostgreSQL?
expected_answer: TRUNCATE and the table-rewriting forms of ALTER TABLE.

spans.quote:
Some DDL commands, currently only TRUNCATE and the table-rewriting forms of ALTER TABLE, are
not MVCC-safe.

question: What is the strictest transaction isolation level supported in PostgreSQL hot standby mode?
notes: Close distractor: the 13.4.1 warning that Serializable protection does not extend to hot standby or logical replicas (does not name the strictest level).
expected_answer: Repeatable Read; Serializable is not yet supported on hot standby replication targets.

spans.quote:
Support for the Serializable transaction isolation level has not yet been added to hot standby replication
targets (described in Section 26.4). The strictest isolation level currently supported in hot standby mode is
Repeatable Read.

question: What happens to a Repeatable Read transaction in PostgreSQL that tries to update a row that a concurrent transaction has already updated and committed?
notes: The evidence is split into two units around a PDF page break ('546 / Concurrency Control'); the page-break noise is excluded from both spans. Close distractor: the Read Committed passage on a second updater.
expected_answer: It is rolled back with the error 'could not serialize access due to concurrent update'.

spans.quote:
But if the first updater commits (and actually updated or deleted
the row, not just locked it) then the repeatable read transaction will be rolled back with the message
ERROR:  could not serialize access due to concurrent update

question: For a multicolumn B-tree index, which query constraints are always used to limit the portion of the index that is scanned?
expected_answer: Equality constraints on leading columns, plus any inequality constraints on the first column that does not have an equality constraint.

spans.quote:
The exact rule is that equality constraints on leading columns, plus any inequality constraints on the first
column that does not have an equality constraint, will always be used to limit the portion of the index that
is scanned.

question: What do BRIN indexes store, and for which kind of columns are they most effective?
expected_answer: They store summaries about the values in consecutive physical block ranges of a table, and are most effective for columns whose values are well-correlated with the physical order of the table rows.

spans.quote:
BRIN indexes (a shorthand for Block Range INdexes) store summaries about the values stored in
consecutive physical block ranges of a table. Thus, they are most effective for columns whose values are
well-correlated with the physical order of the table rows.

question: How many collations can a single PostgreSQL index column support, and what is needed if queries use several collations?
notes: Close distractor: Section 11.10 on operator classes for non-C locales (a different problem: pattern matching).
expected_answer: Only one collation per index column; multiple indexes may be needed if several collations are of interest.

spans.quote:
An index can support only one collation per index column. If multiple collations are of interest, multiple
indexes may be needed.

question: What should be run before examining index usage for an application's queries, and what does it provide?
expected_answer: Run ANALYZE first; it collects statistics about the distribution of the values in the table.

spans.quote:
Always run ANALYZE first. This command collects statistics about the distribution of the values in the
table.

question: In what order does a PostgreSQL B-tree index store its entries by default, with respect to sort direction and nulls?
expected_answer: In ascending order with nulls last (the table TID is a tiebreaker among otherwise equal entries).

spans.quote:
By default, B-tree indexes store their entries in ascending order with nulls last (table TID is treated as a
tiebreaker column among otherwise equal entries).

question: Docker Compose का इस्तेमाल करके जब किसी ऐप को एक ही सर्वर पर चलाना हो, तो किन परिस्थितियों में एक ही कंटेनर के अंदर Uvicorn के कई worker चलाना सही रहता है?

question: docker compose up से एप्लिकेशन और डेटाबेस सर्विस साथ शुरू करने पर विफलता की संभावना क्यों रहती है?

question: PostgreSQL में एक समय में कितनी rows लॉक की जा सकती हैं, और row लॉक करने का क्या अतिरिक्त प्रभाव हो सकता है?
expected_answer: There is no limit on the number of rows locked at one time, but locking a row might cause a disk write (SELECT FOR UPDATE marks the selected rows as locked).

spans.quote:
PostgreSQL doesn't remember any information about modified rows in memory, so there is no limit on
the number of rows locked at one time. However, locking a row might cause a disk write, e.g., SELECT
FOR UPDATE modifies selected rows to mark them locked, and so will result in disk writes.

question: PostgreSQL में यह सुनिश्चित करने के लिए कि कोई concurrent ट्रांज़ैक्शन चुनी गई row को अपडेट या डिलीट न करे, SELECT FOR UPDATE के अलावा क्या करना पड़ता है?
expected_answer: You must actually update the row, even if no values need to be changed; SELECT FOR UPDATE only blocks other transactions temporarily until the lock holder commits or rolls back.

spans.quote:
Also of note to those converting from other environments is the fact that SELECT FOR UPDATE does not
ensure that a concurrent transaction will not update or delete a selected row. To do that in PostgreSQL you
must actually update the row, even if no values need to be changed.

question: PostgreSQL में multicolumn GIN इंडेक्स का इस्तेमाल करते समय, क्या सर्च की performance इस बात से प्रभावित होती है कि query में इंडेक्स के कौन-से कॉलम इस्तेमाल किए गए हैं?
notes: Close distractors: the multicolumn B-tree, GiST and BRIN paragraphs of the same section.
expected_answer: It does not depend on it: unlike B-tree or GiST, GIN search effectiveness is the same regardless of which index columns the query conditions use.

spans.quote:
A multicolumn GIN index can be used with query conditions that involve any subset of the index's columns.
Unlike B-tree or GiST, index search effectiveness is the same regardless of which index column(s) the
query conditions use.

question: PostgreSQL में partial index बनाते समय, सामान्य (common) मानों को इंडेक्स से बाहर रखने का क्या फायदा है?
expected_answer: To reduce the index size, speed up queries that do use the index, and speed up many table update operations, because common values are not indexed.

spans.quote:
One major reason for using a partial index is to avoid indexing common values. Since a query searching
for a common value (one that accounts for more than a few percent of all the table rows) will not use
the index anyway, there is no point in keeping those rows in the index at all. This reduces the size of the
index, which will speed up those queries that do use the index. It will also speed up many table update
operations because the index does not need to be updated in all cases.
